title: Homestead — Platform health
description: Is the control plane itself healthy, and is it telling the truth? Reads the platform's own PostgreSQL tables (ingest dead letters, current-state staleness, command audit, alarms, registry, commissioning) plus Prometheus for scrape health. See deploy/prometheus/prometheus.yml for what Prometheus actually scrapes today.

panels.title: Open alarms by severity
panels.description: States detected, active, acknowledged and mitigated. Cleared and reviewed alarms are history, not open work.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE severity = 'emergency') AS emergency, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE severity = 'critical') AS critical, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE severity = 'major') AS major, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE severity = 'warning') AS warning, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE severity = 'info') AS info FROM alarms WHERE state IN ('detected', 'active', 'acknowledged', 'mitigated')

panels.title: Open alarms
panels.description: SDD 14.3 requires each alarm to link to an operating procedure, the affected asset and its manual controls. That linkage lives in the alarm definition and is shown in the twin UI; this table is the operational queue.

targets.rawSql: SELECT detected_at, severity, state, alarm_key, asset_id, message, suppressed, notified FROM alarms WHERE state IN ('detected', 'active', 'acknowledged', 'mitigated') ORDER BY CASE severity WHEN 'emergency' THEN 0 WHEN 'critical' THEN 1 WHEN 'major' THEN 2 WHEN 'warning' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END, detected_at DESC LIMIT 100

panels.title: Samples written to the historian
panels.description: Rows landing in telemetry_samples. A flat line at zero with a live broker means ingest is resolving nothing — check the dead-letter panel, not the sensors.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ts, $__interval), quality AS metric, COUNT(*) AS value FROM telemetry_samples WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Ingest dead letters
panels.description: Nothing is dropped silently: anything that cannot be resolved to a registry point lands here with a reason. During commissioning this is the most useful table on the property — a silently discarded message looks exactly like a dead sensor.

targets.rawSql: SELECT reason, COUNT(*) AS occurrences, MIN(created_at) AS first_seen, MAX(created_at) AS last_seen, MAX(topic) AS example_topic FROM ingest_dead_letters WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY reason ORDER BY occurrences DESC LIMIT 50

panels.title: Stale and bad-quality points (all domains)
panels.description: Points whose last value is not 'good', or is older than the point's own stale_after_s. This is the platform admitting what it does not currently know (SDD 26.6).

targets.rawSql: SELECT a.domain, cs.point_id, cs.quality, cs.source, cs.ts, ROUND(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - cs.ts))::numeric, 0) AS age_s, cs.stale_after_s FROM current_state cs JOIN assets a ON a.asset_id = cs.asset_id WHERE cs.quality <> 'good' OR cs.ts IS NULL OR (cs.stale_after_s IS NOT NULL AND cs.ts < now() - make_interval(secs => cs.stale_after_s)) ORDER BY a.domain, cs.ts NULLS FIRST LIMIT 200

panels.title: Commands by outcome
panels.description: Every supervisory command and its terminal state. Rejections are not failures of the platform — Level 1 and Level 0 retain the authority to refuse (SDD 6). A rising 'expired' count is: it means acknowledgements are not coming back.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(issued_at, $__interval), state AS metric, COUNT(*) AS value FROM commands WHERE $__timeFilter(issued_at) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Recent commands
panels.description: Who asked, why, under which operating mode, and what happened. issued_by_kind distinguishes a human operator from the EMS or a rule.

targets.rawSql: SELECT issued_at, state, asset_id, command, issued_by, issued_by_kind, operating_mode, reason, state_reason FROM commands WHERE $__timeFilter(issued_at) ORDER BY issued_at DESC LIMIT 100

panels.title: Registry contents
panels.description: Zero here means the design package has not been loaded: run 'chaos load-all'.

targets.rawSql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM assets) AS assets, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM points) AS points, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM point_bindings) AS bindings, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM alarm_definitions) AS alarm_defs, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM power_load_profiles) AS load_profiles

panels.title: Point bindings by status
panels.description: SDD 47: a binding stays 'tbd' until commissioning verifies the real address. This table is the honest measure of how much of the property is actually wired up, as opposed to modelled.

targets.rawSql: SELECT binding_status, COUNT(*) AS bindings, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE automatic_control_allowed) AS automatic_control_allowed, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE commissioned_at IS NOT NULL) AS commissioned FROM point_bindings GROUP BY binding_status ORDER BY bindings DESC

panels.title: Commissioning progress by asset
panels.description: The SDD section 19 twelve-step sequence, per asset. Steps 1-8 plus step 9 must pass before automatic supervisory control is permitted for that asset (maintenance/commissioning.py enforces this).

targets.rawSql: SELECT asset_id, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE result = 'pass') AS passed, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE result = 'fail') AS failed, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE result IS NULL OR result = 'not_run') AS not_run, BOOL_AND(result = 'pass') FILTER (WHERE step <= 9) AS supervisory_control_permitted, MAX(performed_at) AS last_activity FROM commissioning_records GROUP BY asset_id ORDER BY passed DESC, asset_id LIMIT 100

panels.title: Scrape targets up
panels.description: Only Prometheus itself is scraped today. Every other job in deploy/prometheus/prometheus.yml is commented out because its exporter is not deployed or its address is an open item.

panels.title: Scrape target availability
panels.description: up{} per job. A gap here means Prometheus itself lost the target, which on this property usually means the rack lost power or the network.

options.content:
SDD section 8.7 asks Prometheus to cover servers and VMs, switches and access points, UPS and PDUs, NetBotz, storage arrays and ZFS pools, application services, gateway health and backup jobs. **None of those are being scraped today.** Each needs an exporter that is not deployed, and most need a management address that `data/homestead_asset_register.yaml` deliberately records as TBD.

The digital twin API does **not** expose `/metrics`. Application-level health on this dashboard comes from PostgreSQL, which is where the platform actually records what it did.

The two jobs that would change this dashboard most, in order: `snmp_exporter` against the UPS, PDUs and NetBotz on VLAN 10, and `node_exporter` on the R740xd and on the secondary control node.
